target_customer: Engineering teams at large companies with big self-hosted codebases, plus AI coding agents that need code context
problem: Understanding code, not writing it, is the bottleneck for large engineering teams, and AI agents lack context across many repositories.
business_model: Open core (fair source) self-hosted software: free tier up to 5 users, Pro at 20 USD per user per month billed yearly, custom Enterprise
product_category: Code search and code understanding for developers

founders.name: Brendan Kellam
prior_employers: Microsoft (Xbox Cloud Gaming, Visual Studio search)

competitors.name: Sourcegraph
competitors.what: Code search and code intelligence platform; Sourcebot launched as an open source self-hosted alternative built on the Zoekt engine that Sourcegraph maintains

technical_complexity.rationale: Built on the existing Zoekt trigram index, so the core search was not novel. Hard parts were connectors to many code hosts, permission syncing, and later LLM based Ask and MCP features.

defensibility.rationale: Open source code and an engine maintained by a competitor make copying easy. Enterprise integrations and self-hosted deployment add modest stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent code hosts and AI tools kept adding code search and context features. No acquisition of Sourcebot found as of 2026-11.

market_need_then: Large companies needed to search millions of lines across many repos and AI agents needed codebase context. The company says NVIDIA, Red Hat, Wikimedia and Arista engineers use it, and its site quotes a Red Hat security engineer.

branding.domain_note: Uses sourcebot.dev rather than a .com; legal entity is Taqla Inc.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and plain, aimed at engineers.

branding.community_and_virality: Show HN launch in 2024 and an r/opensource post in 2024-10; open source GitHub project with several unrelated repos using the same name.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear and descriptive name that signals a self-hosted source search tool, with some open source community presence, but no distinctive identity or press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Sourcebot started as an open source Sourcegraph alternative in September 2024 and joined YC in Fall 2025, then added AI Ask and MCP features for agents around October 2025. A search result says it moved to a fair source license in March 2026, which would narrow the open source positioning. It is active with named enterprise users, but no priced round or revenue figure is public.
notes: Aggregators (VCBacked, others) report a 500K USD seed from YC dated 2025-09 or 2025-01; unverified so no round recorded. A TechCrunch item surfaced saying Winter 2024 batch which conflicts with the YC page Fall 2025 and is treated as an outlier. License claim (MIT vs fair source, March 2026) comes from a search snippet and was not verified in the repository. Traction and funding of Sourcegraph at the time were not retrieved.
